title: The Engineer’s Daily
subtitle: A daily practice of faith and craft.
goal: A place for people who already code to practice engineering alongside Scripture, prayer and reflection. Over a series, the learner builds and grows a real application whose changes matter to an unfolding fantasy harbor world.
audience: For experienced developers. The first person I am designing for is myself.
current: B2 Coastal Practice is selected. One Beacon lesson is built locally for review.
next: Try the lesson as a daily ritual, refine the stopping point and return path, and connect the wider website around it.

stages.title: Make the work feel grounded
stages.summary: The early studies put Mara and Eli at an ordinary workstation in the harbor. The clear-line illustration gave the story a consistent visual language while keeping recognizable engineering work in view.
stages.decision: Carry forward the characters, harbor setting and believable tools.

artifacts.title: The harbor workstation
artifacts.caption: An early clear-line study, preserved September 8. The terminal is drawn, not a captured application screen.
artifacts.alt: Two illustrated engineers using an Ubuntu workstation beside a harbor window.

stages.title: Stay in one room
stages.summary: The motion study explored moving between the story, a monitor for coding, and reflection without leaving the same illustrated space. It made the lesson feel like a place to spend time.
stages.decision: Keep purposeful motion as an interaction reference. The study does not execute code.

artifacts.title: The continuous room
artifacts.kind: Illustration used in a local prototype
artifacts.caption: The panorama behind the motion study. This image shows the artwork, not the interactive controls.
artifacts.alt: A wide harbor room with Mara, a central computer monitor, Eli and an open journal.

stages.title: Find the invitation
stages.summary: The first full-page concept made the purpose easy to understand. Three alternatives explored a darker night watch, an open coastal layout, and a quieter field journal.
stages.decision: The first layout communicated the activity most clearly. B had the strongest visual appeal, but needed to make the coding more obvious.

artifacts.alt: Warm illustrated full-page website concept for The Engineer’s Daily.

stages.title: B2: the direction to build from
stages.summary: B2 kept the open coastal aesthetic and gave the learning sequence and code preview more presence. That combination became the selected template.
stages.decision: Selected: Coastal Practice. This settles the visual direction, not every generated word, code sample or feature shown in the image.

stages.title: Turn the direction into one daily lesson
stages.summary: A local Beacon Day 12 prototype now connects arrival, coding practice and reflection. It brings the selected visual direction into an actual page, using the motion study as its interaction reference.
stages.decision: Next: review the lesson as a daily practice with its first user. Persistent progress and code execution remain unbuilt; daily return is a goal to test.
